title: Скандал с солью и рассказ Елене  (The Salt Scandal and Telling Elena)

segments.t: Furious that a guest walked out, Vika brings the ruined dish back into the kitchen and demands that Chef Barinov find out who dumped salt on it. Moments later, that very same guest visits Arcobaleno and tells Elena Pavlovna that Claude Monet's kitchen is falling apart without Barinov.
Из-за него у нас гость ушел.
Знаете, не стал дожидаться возвращения Виктора Петровича.
Принесли мне блюда с горой соли.
Alright, let's go through it step by step in English.
'In your opinion, is this normal?' The grammar packs 'wife' and 'fine' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'Who did this?' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'who' and finishing on 'to do'.
Из-за него у нас гость ушел.
'Because of him, a guest walked out on us.' Notice how Russian expresses 'because of' and 'left' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Max answers right away.
'I will get to the bottom of this.' In Russian, the idea of 'I' flows naturally into 'will sort out' without extra filler words.
'That is right.' In Russian, the idea of 'there you go' flows naturally into 'exactly' without extra filler words.
'Or did I ruin the dish myself?' The meaning hinges on 'or' working together with 'takes it back' in spoken Russian. Max answers right away.
'Well, he left, big deal.' In Russian, the idea of 'come on' flows naturally into 'both' without extra filler words.
'Go back to work.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'go' and finishing on 'work'.
Знаете, не стал дожидаться возвращения Виктора Петровича.
'You know, I decided not to wait for Viktor Petrovich to return.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'know' and finishing on 'Petrovich'. Max answers right away.
'As it turned out, that was a big mistake.' The grammar packs 'how' and 'for nothing' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'I was just at Claude Monet.' Chef Viktor brings out the contrast between 'only' and 'what' in a few short words.
Принесли мне блюда с горой соли.
'They brought me a dish buried under a mountain of salt.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'brought' and finishing on 'salt'. Max answers right away.

'Their kitchen must be falling apart without him.' In Russian, the idea of 'probably' flows naturally into 'kitchen' without extra filler words. Alright, let's listen to all those lines again from the top.
Из-за него у нас гость ушел.
Знаете, не стал дожидаться возвращения Виктора Петровича.
Принесли мне блюда с горой соли.
